items.text: US stocks fell to start the week: Dow −0.7% to 51,481.51, S&P 500 −0.8% to 7,683.69, Nasdaq −0.9% to 26,820.38.
The US–Iran standoff pushed Brent crude back to around $106; the 10-year Treasury yield hit a nearly two-decade high and traders raised bets on an October Fed rate hike.

Fed Governor Lisa Cook said AI may eventually lower inflation but won't stop the price pressures that led the Fed to raise rates. PCE inflation (Wed), manufacturing (Thu) and the September jobs report (Fri) are due this week.
The US and China said they agreed to a $30 billion reciprocal tariff reduction and to open a bilateral dialogue on AI.
Asia fell on higher oil: South Korea's Kospi −2.7%, China's CSI 300 −2.2%, Japan's Nikkei −0.7%; Hong Kong's Hang Seng edged up.
UK housebuilders jumped at the open (Taylor Wimpey +23%, Vistry +20%) after the Labour government announced a scheme for first-time buyers.
Australia: Northern Star Resources rejected an unsolicited $38 billion takeover offer from a South African rival; the Reserve Bank is widely expected to raise rates to 4.6% on Tuesday.
Nvidia shares rose after the company approved a record $150 billion stock buyback, even as the wider tech sector slid.
AMD became the first woman-led company worth $1 trillion.
A US jury ordered Apple to pay Taction more than $5.7 billion over haptic-technology patents; Apple denies infringing and plans to appeal.
China is reportedly tightening travel limits on AI researchers and chip engineers, treating them as strategic national assets.
Micron reports fiscal Q4 results Wednesday, a key read on AI chip demand.
Boeing fell about 6% to a 2026 low after reports the FAA is delaying certification of the 737 Max 10 over a navigation software issue.
President Trump is set to announce plans for a $15 billion steel plant, which would be the largest in the US.
Paramount Skydance rose 3.8% after announcing $44.4 billion in secured notes to help fund its purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery.
Kodiak Sciences soared about 155% on positive Phase 3 results for two wet macular degeneration treatments.
Shein reports its first earnings as a public company; the stock is down roughly 28% since listing amid slowing demand and rising costs.
Wall Street sentiment on Nike is at its lowest in at least 25 years after Bank of America turned negative on the sportswear maker.
Armani's CEO said the group is open to several investors sharing the 15% stake set aside for sale in Giorgio Armani's will.
Wells Fargo upgraded Sweetgreen to overweight with an $11 target, up from Friday's $8.24 close.
Mars Wrigley will close its Newark, NJ candy plant in October, cutting 307 jobs; Nestlé Purina is investing about $640 million in a pet-food plant in Mantova, Italy.
Hormel named president John Ghingo as CEO effective October 26.
Saudi Arabia is collecting a large oil windfall from the Iran conflict as crude stays above $100.
